title: Every actions/create-github-app-token step must set explicit owner and bare repository names
answers: actions/create-github-app-token step rejected by policy: owner or repositories missing
how do I scope a GitHub App token to a repository in MLflow workflows
why does conftest deny my create-github-app-token step without repositories
GitHub App installation token not restricted to specific repos
body:
Invariant: every `actions/create-github-app-token` step must set a non-empty `with.owner` and `with.repositories`. Omitting either leaves the token unscoped, so the policy denies it.
Enforced by: .github/policy.rego:deny_create_app_token_without_repository_scope. It loops over the keys {owner, repositories} and denies when `trim(value, " \t\n") == ""`, so blank and whitespace-only values also fail.
Value format: `repositories` takes bare repository names, comma-separated (e.g. `mlflow` or `mlflow,internal`). It does not take `owner/repo`. `${{ github.repository }}` expands to `mlflow/mlflow` and matches no repository, so use literals.
Constraints: the check only tests that the raw YAML value is non-empty. It does not verify that an expression resolves to a real repository at runtime.
What breaks: a step that sets only `owner`, or only `repositories`, is still denied, since each key is checked separately.
applies: Any workflow or composite action in this repository that mints a GitHub App token with actions/create-github-app-token. Current MLflow values are owner `mlflow` and repositories `mlflow`, or `mlflow,internal` for Nailaopus.
says: Pull request validation pipeline failed on security policy for generating access tokens.
Build check failed because the application token request did not specify allowed repositories.
Continuous integration fails compliance checks when minting unscoped application credentials.
Require workflow installation tokens to restrict access to explicitly named target projects.
search: Policy enforcement in .github/policy.rego:deny_create_app_token_without_repository_scope requires every actions/create-github-app-token step to set non-empty with.owner and with.repositories. It applies to workflows and composite actions minting GitHub App tokens, where repositories must be comma-separated bare repository names such as mlflow or mlflow,internal rather than owner/repo or ${{ github.repository }}. The check tests only that raw YAML values are non-empty after trimming whitespace, denying steps if either key is missing or blank, without verifying runtime repository resolution.
